target_name: Flow And State Hard Tilt Combined
rationale: This is a mechanical SUMRANK blend of the two strongest archive constructs and is very close in spirit to the already-tested gen-8 level-plus-state consolidation; moreover the claim of conceptual independence is doubtful, since a firm typically reaches its five-year hard-tilt extreme precisely by executing the one-year reallocation the flow leg measures, so the two ranks will be highly correlated and the composite is likely to deliver a cosmetic averaging of existing results rather than new information.

target_name: Hard Tilt Against Gross Profit Capacity
rationale: A single-deflator swap on the champion is a modest refinement rather than a new mechanism, but the argument that smoothed gross profit is time-varying and encodes margin compression (whereas the previously rejected capital-stock deflator was near-constant within firm) is coherent, and the TS_RANK wrapper neutralizes cross-sectional gross-profitability level so the test is not a disguised Novy-Marx rediscovery.

target_name: Hard Tilt State Under Demand Uncertainty
rationale: The real-options rationale is sound and the sign is internally consistent, but this is the third pairing of five-year sales-growth volatility with a hard-versus-soft investment measure in the archive, and since volatile-demand firms already carry their own return tilt there is a real risk the VOL leg, not the champion state, drives whatever alpha appears.

target_name: Soft Tilt Event And State With Profit Delivery
rationale: This is the mirror image of proposal one multiplied by an unchanged profit-growth screen, so it inherits the same correlated-parents problem while adding no new conditioning economics — both parent specifications already exist in the archive with near-identical fmb and alpha, and averaging them is precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against.

target_name: Soft Tilt State With Rising Labor Productivity
rationale: Swapping the validation leg from aggregate gross-profit growth to scale-free gross profit per employee is a substantive discriminating test of whether the long-side result is a growth artifact or a genuine productivity effect, and the archive gives real reason for doubt since the per-employee leg has previously produced a positive slope with a negative portfolio alpha in a different pairing.

Differencing the within-firm rank is a genuinely distinct object from both the dollar-denominated flow measure and the standing state, and it cleanly decomposes whether the champion's predictive content is positional or transitional; the main caveat is that a five-period TS_RANK is coarse, so the difference will be a noisy few-level step and coverage/turnover diagnostics deserve attention.
